I want the best bang for the buck, not the cheapest or the most expensive.

That makes total sense, especially with roses and perennials being an investment.

When we talk about “best bang for the buck” with our plants, I usually look at:

How long and often it blooms (repeat or continual bloom = more value)
How healthy and disease resistant it tends to be (less time and money fixing problems)
How well it fits your climate and sun (so it thrives long term, not just this year)

turns.replyText:
Honestly, is the pricier one worth the extra, or is the cheaper one fine?

Totally get where you’re coming from, especially if money’s tight – you want to know if you’ll feel the difference, not just pay for a higher price tag.

Whether the pricier one is “worth it” really depends on the specific plants you’re looking at, because the extra cost can sometimes mean:

Better disease resistance / longer life
Stronger repeat blooming
Bigger or more unique flowers
Stronger fragrance

But other times, the more affordable option is absolutely solid and the upgrade is more about small extras than a real quality jump.
